business_problem: Universal Robots needed to move collaborative robots beyond static programmed tasks so manufacturers in dynamic, high-mix environments could deploy cobots for adaptive assembly and machine-tending work without complex manual reprogramming.
solution_summary: Universal Robots built its AI Accelerator on the NVIDIA Isaac robotics platform to create a physical-AI stack for adaptive cobots. The platform runs on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin at the edge and combines NVIDIA Isaac Manipulator components such as cuMotion, FoundationPose, and FoundationStereo with Isaac ROS, Isaac Lab, and NITROS integration for ROS 2 environments. In production, the cobot stack handles real-time object recognition, 3D pose estimation, motion planning, and low-latency perception-to-control handoff without depending on the cloud. In development, Universal Robots uses Isaac Lab and simulated training with domain randomization to build reinforcement-learning policies that transfer to real assembly tasks without manual fine-tuning. This architecture lets the company package advanced AI perception and motion into an accessible cobot platform instead of forcing each customer to build custom robotics pipelines from scratch.

data_flow: Sensors and cameras feed perception into the AI Accelerator on Jetson AGX Orin, Isaac Manipulator modules estimate pose and plan motion, ROS-based control loops execute adaptive robot actions, and simulation-trained policies from Isaac Lab move into real cobot tasks with minimal extra tuning.
business_outcome: Universal Robots achieved up to 100x faster motion planning, enabled accurate 3D pose estimation with minimal training, shortened partner time to market for AI-powered cobot solutions, and opened new application categories and revenue streams across industrial automation.
